role.altitude: The law lecturer keeps analysing law, writing, lecturing, discussing and signing off grades; searching database by database, scanning newsletters, typing case summaries and entering grades twice shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking drafted case summaries against the judgment text
role.ambitious_version: A lecturer whose records keep themselves, leaving the hours for scholarship and students.

tasks.short: Search case law, legislation and literature, analyse sources and develop the argument, write the article or book, and submit and handle peer review to conduct research and publish findings.

steps.what: Lecturer searches case law, legislation and literature for the research topic

loop.input: The research question and the legal and literature databases.
loop.output: A list of relevant judgments, provisions and articles with short summaries.
loop.check: Every judgment must resolve to its official identifier and every article to the catalogue or a DOI; the lecturer checks each summary against the source and reads each source used.
loop.stop: Unresolvable items are dropped; the lecturer ends the search when no new relevant sources appear.
loop.why_not_simpler: Legal terms differ across jurisdictions and periods.

steps.what: Lecturer reads the sources and develops the legal analysis
Lecturer writes the article or book chapter with citations
Lecturer checks the final manuscript: the argument, citations and quoted law are right
Lecturer submits the checked manuscript to the journal or publisher
Lecturer responds to peer review

tasks.design: A search step lists relevant judgments, provisions and articles with short summaries, and every item must resolve to its official identifier or the catalogue before the lecturer reads it. Analysis and the argument stay with the lecturer. A reference manager formats citations to the legal citation guide, so the writing itself changes little. Peer review stays as it is.

approvals.approved_version: The manuscript exactly as checked by the lecturer in s3b, submitted once to the named journal or publisher; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Searches went database by database and citations were formatted by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Literature tools with summaries, identifier checks and reference managers.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing the tension between two lines of case law.
tasks.altitude: Less searching and formatting; scholarship stays.

evidence.claim: A literature database tool gives topic summaries and foundational papers.

assumptions: Boundary: research and publishing; keeping abreast of the field (task 6220) and compiling reading lists (task 6232) are sibling tasks.
Analysis and peer review keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of sources in indexed databases.
research_questions: Does the first search round take less time without missing key cases?

incremental.description: Lecturer reports summaries that misstate a source.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: much of the topic rests on older or unindexed sources, so s1 keeps 90 (4.7); high: well-indexed sources as assumed (9.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Scan new case law, legislation and journals, read key items in depth, and talk with colleagues and attend conferences to keep abreast of developments in the field.

steps.what: Lecturer scans new case law, legislation and current literature
Lecturer reads key judgments and articles in depth
Lecturer talks with colleagues and participates in professional conferences

tasks.design: Saved searches in the legal databases send alerts for new judgments, legislation and articles on the lecturer's topics, with links to the official text, instead of scanning several newsletters in full. Reading in depth, talking with colleagues and conferences stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: News came through many newsletters and database visits.
tasks.enabler_now: Saved searches and alerts in legal databases.
tasks.still_hard: Developments discussed only in practitioner circles.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting which new judgment will matter.
tasks.altitude: Less scanning; reading and talking stay.

reach.learn: Whether lectures include new case law sooner.

evidence.claim: Legal and literature databases offer saved searches with alerts.

assumptions: Boundary: keeping abreast; research for publications (task 6223) is a sibling task.
Reading in depth and conferences keep their full time.
unknowns: How many sources the lecturer follows.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: alerts miss the commentary in newsletters, which are still scanned, so s1 keeps 85 (4.9); high: alerts replace most scanning as assumed (10.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record attendance, enter grades, transfer grades to the student system, check and sign off grade lists, and keep extension and exemption records to maintain student attendance records, grades and other required records.

steps.what: Students check in to the session with the code in the learning platform
Lecturer records student attendance: on a paper list today; after the change students check in with a code and the lecturer confirms the list
Lecturer enters grades in the learning platform gradebook
Lecturer transfers grades to the student information system: typing them again today; after the change a sync sends them and the lecturer fixes those it rejects
Lecturer checks the final grade list in the student system as examiner: each grade matches the gradebook and the exam decisions
Lecturer signs off the checked grade list, which makes the grades final
Student submits an extension or exemption request on the platform form
Lecturer records extensions and exemptions: from mails today; after the change the lecturer decides on each request form in the platform and marks it

tasks.design: Students check in to compulsory sessions with a code in the learning platform, so attendance is recorded without a paper list. Marks from the assessment tool flow into the gradebook, and a sync sends final grades to the student information system, ending the double entry. The examiner checks the grade list in the student system and signs it off once, which makes the grades final. Extension and exemption requests come in through a form in the platform and are recorded there. No software sets a grade.

approvals.approved_version: The grade list per student exactly as checked by the examiner in s4, signed off once in the student information system, which makes the grades final; any change needs a new check and sign-off.

tasks.previous_blocker: Grades were entered twice and attendance kept on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Gradebook syncs to student information systems and platform check-in.
tasks.still_hard: Oral exams and moot courts graded on paper.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a grade that cannot be right for that student.
tasks.altitude: Much less record keeping; signing off stays.

evidence.claim: A university requires grades from the learning platform always also be published in the student system, which means double entry.
Examiners appointed by the examination board set results.

assumptions: Boundary: keeping records; grading work (task 6215) and exams (task 6216) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s2: marks from the assessment tool used for exams and assignments.

Checking and signing off keep their full time. s1 keeps 30 for confirming the list and late arrivals; s3 keeps 10 for grades the sync rejects; s5 keeps 60 for deciding and marking each request. The students' check-in and request form are shown in s0 and s4c.
unknowns: Whether the university allows a gradebook sync.

incremental.description: No new work: fixing sync errors is priced in s3.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of the sessions still use paper lists, so s1 keeps 65 (51.7); high: online check-in as assumed (58.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select new case law and legislation to cover, prepare slides and case summaries, deliver lectures on topics such as civil procedure, contracts and torts, and answer questions.

steps.what: Lecturer selects new case law and legislation to cover in the lectures
Lecturer prepares slides and case summaries

loop.input: The selected judgments with their official identifiers.
loop.output: Draft case summaries: facts, question, holding and reasoning.
loop.check: Every quoted holding must match the judgment text word for word; the lecturer checks that each summary states the holding and the reasoning correctly, and edits it.
loop.stop: The lecturer keeps a summary, or writes it by hand when the draft misreads the case.
loop.why_not_simpler: Judgments vary in structure and length.

steps.what: Lecturer delivers lectures on civil procedure, contracts or torts
Lecturer answers students' questions after the lecture

tasks.design: Choosing which new law to cover stays with the lecturer, using the alerts from keeping abreast of the field. A drafting step writes case summaries from the judgments, with every quoted holding matching the judgment text, and the lecturer edits them into the slides. Lecturing and answering questions stay fully personal.
tasks.previous_blocker: Case summaries were written from scratch for each update.
tasks.enabler_now: Drafting from official judgment texts with quote checks.
tasks.human_edge: Making a dry procedural rule come alive with a story.

reach.learn: Whether summaries help them read the full judgments.

evidence.claim: Drafting course materials is not a high-risk use under the AI Act; grading and proctoring are.

assumptions: Boundary: preparing and delivering lectures; preparing syllabi and handouts (task 6219) and moderating discussions (task 6218) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: alerts from task 6220; the search saving is counted there.
Selecting, lecturing and answering keep their full time.
research_questions: Is lecture preparation shorter without poorer summaries?

incremental.description: Lecturer reports summaries that misread a case.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: drafted summaries miss the point of many cases, so s2 keeps 85 (3.4); high: drafts usable after editing as assumed (7.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
